title: Gulati Hopes Rhea Chakraborty Feels Vindicated by 'Pooja Meri Jaan'
excerpt: Director Navjot Gulati says the ZEE5 courtroom drama's media-trial sequences drew from Chakraborty's case, calling the witch hunt against her 'wrong at every level.'
body:
• Director Navjot Gulati says his courtroom drama Pooja Meri Jaan, now streaming on ZEE5, drew directly from the media trial of Rhea Chakraborty after the death of Sushant Singh Rajput.
  • Gulati says he wrote the film before Chakraborty's case but shaped its media-hounding sequences on what happened to her, calling the witch hunt against her "wrong at every level."
  • The Hindi film stars Mrunal Thakur, Huma Qureshi, Vijay Raaz and Vikram Singh Chauhan, and follows a woman prosecuted and publicly shamed after refusing a man's advances.
  • Diaspora viewers can watch it on ZEE5, where it released on October 2 after nearly four years of release delays.
https://youtube.com/watch?v=IDZYIndEa1c

Director Navjot Gulati hopes Rhea Chakraborty watches his film. Speaking about Pooja Meri Jaan, the courtroom drama that released on ZEE5 on October 2, Gulati told Bollywood Hungama that the film's first half — in which its protagonist is hounded by television media and tried on social media — drew from what happened to Chakraborty after she was blamed for abetting the suicide of actor Sushant Singh Rajput. The Indian Express reported Gulati saying he hoped Chakraborty would feel vindicated after watching the film.

"I wrote the film before her case, but was inspired by what happened to her. The witch hunt against her was wrong at every level."

— Navjot Gulati, Director, Pooja Meri Jaan

A film about a woman the system decided was guilty

Pooja Meri Jaan is a Hindi courtroom drama starring Mrunal Thakur and Huma Qureshi, with Vijay Raaz and Vikram Singh Chauhan. It is directed by Gulati and Vipasha Arvind and written by Gulati, Kanishka Singh Deo and Niren Bhatt. Its story turns on a woman who says no to a man, is stalked and harassed, and then finds society — and the legal process — treating her as the accused despite evidence in her favour, a theme reviewers have described as the film's core: a woman saying no, a man not accepting the answer, and a public witch hunt that follows.

Gulati has been careful to say the film is not a side-taking exercise. Some viewers, he acknowledged, came away feeling the girl in his story was in the wrong; his point, he said, was not to declare one gender right, but to show what a media-and-mob trial does to the person inside it — the same machinery that surrounded Chakraborty in 2020, when she was arrested by the Narcotics Control Bureau and spent weeks as the lead story on Indian news channels before the case against her collapsed in court.

Four years on a shelf, then a streaming release

The film's own history mirrors its theme of delayed justice. Backed by Dinesh Vijan's Maddock Films and producer Amar Kaushik, Pooja Meri Jaan finished shooting in 2022 and then waited nearly four years for release as negotiations with streaming platforms repeatedly broke down over acquisition price. Gulati publicly appealed to Maddock Films over the delay and said he did not want the film to meet the fate of Shoojit Sircar's Shoebite, which remains unreleased. It finally reached audiences as part of ZEE5's slate this month.

Gulati says the response has justified the wait. He recounted that a friend's sister, harassed by a man for four years, watched the film and found the courage to tell her family and file a police complaint. "I don't think a film can do much more than have an impact like this in real life," he said. For diaspora audiences, the film is available on ZEE5 internationally — a four-year-old film about a media trial that, its director argues, India has not stopped re-running since.
